rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (FY23): 'In fiscal year 2023, approximately 10% of our total government revenues were generated from cost-reimbursement contracts with the federal government or our prime contractors, less than 1% from time-and-materials contracts and approximately 90% from fixed-price contracts.' Customer concentration around US Government implied; no single-customer >10% explicit threshold disclosed.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the 10-K and post-10-K 10-Qs disclose customer concentration consistent with this composition. Mode B — derive: a satellite operator with US Gov as major customer should disclose ITC/CMMC/CUI compliance status and any pending DCAA/DCMA audit disputes given fixed-price exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K FY23 risk factors + 10-Q Q3FY24 contingencies/DCAA section
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q Q3FY24: DCAA incurred-cost audits open for FY2004, 2016, 2019, 2020, 2021 (FY2021 pending). $16.6M contract-related reserves for refund potential. No single customer >10% threshold disclosed; segment-level USG mix consistent across periods.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Consistent and unremarkable. USG concentration risk acknowledged but not concealed; reserves modest and reserve-only.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (FY23, filed May 22, 2023, before Inmarsat close on May 30, 2023): 'We obtained financing commitments for an additional $1.6 billion of new debt facilities in connection with the Inmarsat Transaction. We also plan to assume $2.1 billion in principal amount of Inmarsat senior secured bonds and the outstanding indebtedness under Inmarsat's $2.4 billion senior secured credit facilities.' Implies pro-forma total debt ~$7B with leverage as a material risk factor.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify post-close 10-Q reconciles to the disclosed pro-forma debt stack. Mode B — derive: at $7B+ debt with negative operating cash flow and 10.94% effective rate on 2023 TLF, near-term maturities (2025 Notes $700M, 2026 Inmarsat TLB $1.68B, 2026 Inmarsat Notes $2.08B) would force a refi well before cutoff. Did management address the 2025–2026 wall?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q Q3FY24 (filed Feb 9, 2024) Note 8 debt table + 8-K 2024-03-28 Refinancing Amendment
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt Dec 31, 2023 = $7.57B (incl Inmarsat 2026 Notes $2.08B, Inmarsat TLB $1.68B). 8-K 2024-03-28: extended $1.75B Inmarsat 2026 TLB by replacing $1.3B with new TLB maturing September 2029, plus $550M undrawn RCF maturing March 2027. $300M residual Inmarsat 2026 TLB. 2025 Notes ($700M) still mature March 2025 — closest wall.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Debt scale confirmed and proactively termed-out — but the 2025 Notes wall is unresolved at cutoff. Company is term-extending under pressure (Amendment No. 4) rather than refinancing from strength.

rfm_tuples.R: 8-K Aug 25, 2023: 'On August 24, 2023, Viasat, Inc. entered into the Seventh Amendment to Credit Agreement [...] The Amendment, among other matters, provides additional covenant flexibility and provides for commitments under the Revolving Credit Agreement in an aggregate amount of $597,500,000.00.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — confirm the amendment exists and is a covenant-flexibility amendment, not merely a maturity extension. Mode B — derive: covenant flex amendments coincident with a material satellite anomaly (July 12 ViaSat-3, Aug 24 I-6 F2 disclosed same day as amendment) signal management foresaw covenant breach risk; check whether subsequent compliance certifications hold.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Aug 25 amendment explicitly grants 'additional covenant flexibility' and was negotiated the same day Viasat publicly disclosed the I-6 F2 anomaly — a clear distressed-debt action. 10-Q Q3FY24 (Dec 31, 2023): 'The Company was in compliance with its financial covenants under the 2022 Term Loan Facility as of December 31, 2023.' Two amendments to the RCF/credit facilities filed before cutoff (Aug 2023 + Mar 2024 refi).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two covenant/refi amendments within 7 months coincident with satellite anomalies and $1.6B impairment is textbook distressed-debt behavior. Compliance certification holds only because covenants were loosened. Pattern: company is solvency-managing, not operating from strength.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-Q Q1FY24 (filed Aug 9, 2023): 'On July 12, 2023, the Company reported a reflector deployment issue that may materially impact the performance of the ViaSat-3 Americas satellite. [...] The ViaSat-3 Americas satellite is insured for approximately $420 million, which is nearly half of the net book value of the ViaSat-3 Americas satellite, including capitalized interest.' Q3FY24 update: 'the Company will recover less than 10% of the planned throughput on the ViaSat-3 F1 satellite.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the impairment was actually recognized and quantified in subsequent quarters as the root-cause analysis matured. Mode B — derive: if the satellite is a near-total loss and is only insured for half NBV, the uninsured shortfall must flow through SG&A as an impairment; check insurance receivable booked vs cash received.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q Q3FY24 Note 1 satellite impairment & related charges + subsequent events
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3FY24 disclosed $1.6B carrying-value reduction on satellites under construction (ViaSat-3 F1, I-6 F2, ViaSat-4 program) net of $770M insurance claim receivables, yielding ~$905.5M net loss in SG&A for the nine months ended Dec 31, 2023. 'Subsequent to the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, the Company received nearly $260 million in insurance recovery proceeds related to such claims.' — cash recovery in progress, matches receivable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Impairment disclosure is honest, sequenced (Q1 'cannot assess' → Q2 quantified → Q3 cash recovery starting). Mode-B derivation that uninsured loss must hit P&L is verified. No concealment; this is a recognized loss event, not a hidden one.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-Q Q3FY24 MD&A: 'we reduced our global workforce by approximately 800 positions, or approximately 10%, and recorded total costs (primarily related to employee severance payments, benefits and related termination costs) of approximately $45 million during the three and nine months ended December 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify size of action and that costs flow through opex. Mode B — derive: a 10% RIF immediately after closing the Inmarsat deal (May 2023) signals integration cost overrun and shrinking opex envelope; check whether headcount/severance scale matches the disclosed combined company size.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 800 positions for $45M = ~$56k/head — consistent with severance economics for a tech/aerospace combined workforce of ~8,000 employees post-Inmarsat (i.e., 10% checks out). 'Insignificant amounts remaining' suggests not a stepwise multi-round RIF (yet).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is internally consistent. Severity-Moderate because the RIF is being framed as 'rationalization' but is in fact a forced cost cut against a $1.6B impairment + 10.94% debt rate — pattern of distress, not pattern of growth-stage scaling.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K FY23 Item 8: 'Report of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (PCAOB ID 238)'.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify Big 4 auditor identity and PCAOB ID. Mode B — derive: a distressed-debt issuer with $1.6B impairment under a Big 4 auditor should have a critical audit matter on satellite carrying value or going-concern emphasis-of-matter; check for any auditor change or resignation 8-K.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K FY23 Item 8 + filings index search for 8-K Item 4.01 (auditor change)
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC LLP, PCAOB ID 238 — Big 4. No 8-K Item 4.01 (auditor change) in the pre-cutoff filing list (43 Form 4s, 14 8-Ks reviewed; no 4.01). No 'going concern' or 'substantial doubt' phrase appears anywhere in the FY23 10-K or any pre-cutoff 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Stable Big 4 auditor, no resignations, no going-concern. This argues against the company being a fraud/late-stage distress candidate; the impairment was disclosed and audited.

rfm_tuples.R: Form 4 activity July 2023 – May 14, 2024 (post-ViaSat-3 anomaly): 43 Form 4 filings, dominated by RSU vests, option exercises, equity grants under the Restated Equity Plan, and small charitable gifts. No insiders filed open-market purchases at the post-anomaly price (range $15–$42).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify there were no Director/Officer open-market BUYS at the distressed price. Mode B — derive: if management/board genuinely believed in the post-impairment franchise (Inmarsat synergies, insurance recoveries), the rational signal would be insider buying; absence is a passive-negative signal.
rfm_tuples.M_source: EDGAR Form 4 stream for CIK 0000797721 (Jul 2023 – May 14, 2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: All transactions are code A (award), M (option exercise/conversion), F (tax withholding), G (gift), or small S (sell to cover). Examples: 2023-07-12 Miller Craig (CTO/founder-class) S 200 sh @$41.90; 2023-10-11 same S 150 sh @$15.38; 2024-04-01 Bridenstine G 1000 (gift); 2024-05-14 Gowrappan (CEO Yahoo, joined board) M+F. No Code P (open-market purchase) by any director/officer during distressed window.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider behavior does not contradict the distressed thesis but does not confirm conviction either. Mode-B derivation (where are the insider buys?) yields a passive negative. Note: founder-CEO Mark Dankberg historically does not open-market trade, so absence is partially structural.

rfm_tuples.R: Claim evolution between 10-Q Q1FY24 (Aug 9, 2023) and 10-Q Q3FY24 (Feb 9, 2024). Q1FY24: 'may materially impact the performance of the ViaSat-3 Americas satellite. [...] not able to assess the impairment value [...] insured for approximately $420 million, which is nearly half of the net book value.' Q3FY24: 'will recover less than 10% of the planned throughput [...] $1.6 billion impairment partially offset by $770 million insurance claim receivables.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — does the trajectory of disclosure show degrading honesty (downplaying) or improving honesty (escalating)? Mode B — derive: claim evolution itself is a forensic signal; if Q1's 'may materially impact' becomes Q3's '<10% recovery,' the company moved from hedged language to a definitive quantification within one quarter, which is the honest path. Compare with Q3FY24's still-pending I-6 F2 narrative.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q Q1FY24 Note 13 Subsequent Event vs 10-Q Q3FY24 Note 1
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosure escalated rather than de-escalated: 'may materially impact' → 'will recover less than 10%' is a transition from hedged to definitive within ~6 months. Insurance recovery moved from claim-pending ($420M coverage) to claim-filed ($770M receivable) to cash-received (~$260M). Q3FY24 added the I-6 F2 total loss to the same impairment bucket — additive bad news, not concealed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Per the Honesty-Alpha framework: this is the textbook honest-disclosure trajectory under stress. Re-detecting losses VSAT itself escalated is not alpha. Honesty here means the framework should EXCLUDE VSAT from the SHORT bucket on lying-detector grounds, even though the underlying business is impaired.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-Q Q3FY24 Note 8: '2023 Term Loan Facility [...] the effective interest rate on the Company's outstanding borrowings under the 2023 Term Loan Facility was 10.94%.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify effective rate. Mode B — derive: a 10.94% all-in cost on $615M of new term loan (May 2023) priced after the Inmarsat close is a stressed-issuer rate; healthier issuers would price closer to SOFR+200–300 bps. Compare to Inmarsat 2026 6.75% legacy notes (priced pre-stress).
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2023 TLF effective rate 10.94% (SOFR+450 with 0.50% floor). March 2024 Refinancing Amendment replaced Inmarsat 2026 TLB at higher pricing into new 2029 TLB. Annualized interest expense Q3FY24 = $133.5M (run-rate ~$534M/yr) vs $8.7M Q3FY23 (pre-Inmarsat) — 15x increase consistent with debt scale + rate hikes.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Confirmed. Cost of debt is at distressed-issuer levels. The company is now structurally a high-fixed-cost levered satellite operator with insurance receivables being deployed to pay down debt; this constrains capex for the next-gen fleet for years.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K FY23 + 10-Q Q3FY24: No 'going concern' or 'substantial doubt' language anywhere in pre-cutoff filings. Compliance certifications repeated every quarter.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — confirm absence of going-concern. Mode B — derive: given $1.6B impairment, $7.57B total debt, $605M FY24 nine-month operating loss before impairment, and forward maturities ($700M 2025 Notes), the lack of going-concern is supportable only if liquidity is genuinely strong; check cash position and RCF availability.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash + short-term investments Dec 31, 2023 = $1,651M ($1,621M cash + $30M STI). Undrawn Viasat RCF $597.5M post-Aug 2023 amendment + undrawn Inmarsat $700M (replaced March 2024 with $550M to March 2027). Pro-forma liquidity ~$2.8B. $700M 2025 Notes mature March 2025 — coverable from cash alone if needed; insurance proceeds ($260M received post-Q3) provide further cushion. Going-concern absence is defensible.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity stack is genuinely sufficient through the 2025 Notes maturity at cutoff. The framework should NOT score this as a fraud/lying-distress case. It is a recognized, audited, transparent impairment with adequate liquidity and proactive (if expensive) refinancing.

summary: Pre-cutoff VSAT 10-K + 3 sequential 10-Qs show a transparent, audited (PwC Big 4) impairment cycle following two satellite anomalies (ViaSat-3 F1 reflector July 2023; I-6 F2 Aug 2023). Management quantified $1.6B impairment net of $770M insurance receivable, recognized losses in SG&A, executed two covenant/refi amendments (Aug 2023 + Mar 2024), did a 10% RIF, and maintained sufficient liquidity (~$2.8B) to cover the March 2025 Notes wall. No going-concern, no auditor change, no Form D/Form 4 distress signal. Claim trajectory escalated rather than de-escalated. Net forensic verdict: this is honest-but-impaired, not a lying-distress profile. Per the Honesty-Alpha framework, the framework's contribution is EXCLUSION from the SHORT bucket — re-detecting bad news the company has already disclosed is not alpha. Two SEVERE flags (covenant flex amendments and 10.94% distressed debt cost) keep this from being a LONG, but the lack of concealment, intact liquidity, and proactive 2029 term-out argue against SHORT.
